info.title: NGP VAN API (community OpenAPI spec)
info.description:
Community-maintained OpenAPI spec for the NGP VAN API, reverse-engineered from https://docs.ngpvan.com, the NGPVAN/van-cli source, and live probing of the sandbox API. The spec describes the API's actual behavior as observed. Where that behavior deviates from the official docs, the comparison is recorded out of band in `x-docs-discrepancy` fields (hidden by most documentation renderers) and summarized in [DISCREPANCIES.md](https://github.com/NickCrews/van-openapi/blob/main/DISCREPANCIES.md); research evidence and confidence notes live in `x-provenance` fields.

Source repository: https://github.com/NickCrews/van-openapi — file issues and corrections there. This spec is not published or endorsed by NGP VAN; for questions about the API itself, contact APIDevelopers@ngpvan.com.

See [STATUS.md](https://github.com/NickCrews/van-openapi/blob/main/STATUS.md) for per-endpoint research status.

**The API is not callable from a browser.** Its CORS support is incomplete: `api.securevan.com` answers the preflight correctly — reflecting the request origin and allowing the `Authorization` header — but omits `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` from the actual response (observed 2026-08-03; a `200` comes back with no `access-control-*` headers at all). A browser therefore sends the request, receives the response, and then blocks the page from reading it. `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials` is missing as well, which Basic auth would separately require. This affects only browser-based callers; server-side clients such as cURL, Python, or Apps Script are unaffected, since CORS is enforced by the browser rather than the server.

get.summary: Get a person by VAN id
get.description: Retrieves a person record. Related collections (emails, phones, addresses, …) are null unless requested via $expand, and empty arrays when expanded but absent. An unknown, zero, or negative vanId returns the standard 404 error envelope; a non-integer path segment does not match the route and returns an HTML 404 page instead.

parameters.name: vanId
parameters.description: VAN id of the person.
parameters.x-docs-discrepancy: Official docs type this path parameter as string (default "100476252"); the route only matches integers — a non-integer segment returns an IIS HTML 404 page (observed 2026-08-03).

parameters.name: $expand
parameters.description: Related sections to include, comma-delimited eg 'addresses,emails'. Anything outside this set returns 400 INVALID_PARAMETER with a hint listing the valid values. Two sections in the set are still refused in a My Campaign context: `scores` with 403 FORBIDDEN and `pollingLocation` with 400 BAD_REQUEST.
parameters.x-docs-discrepancy: Official docs list only 10 valid $expand values; the API's own INVALID_PARAMETER hint (observed 2026-08-03) lists these 23.

200.description: The person record. Clients that follow redirects can also land here with `text/html` instead: a path segment containing `<`, `>`, `*` or `&` is bounced to the web application's error page, which answers 200 with HTML (see the 302 response).

expanded.summary: Sandbox test person with $expand=emails,phones,addresses (abridged: null-only fields omitted)

x-provenance.note: The VAN web app's "Oops...something went wrong" page, reached by following the request-validation 302. Documented so redirect-following clients (including the schemathesis stateful phase, which found it) conform.

post.description:
Merges the payload into an existing record. Fields left out of the body keep their current values, and `emails`, `phones` and `addresses` are appended to what is already there rather than replacing it — there is no way to remove a contact method through this endpoint. An empty body is accepted and changes nothing.

On success the response is **302 Found** with a `Location` header pointing back at `/people/{vanId}` and a match-stub body — the same shape POST /people/find returns, not the updated record. An unknown, zero or negative vanId returns 404.

The update is not idempotent for contact methods: sending the same email twice adds it twice.

x-provenance.note: Merge semantics confirmed by updating only middleName on a record and observing firstName, lastName and employer survive; append semantics by adding a second email and seeing both returned, with isPreferred moving to the newer one. Not in the official docs' page index; the path comes from van-cli (people.ts update), which notes PUT is not supported.

parameters.name: vanId
parameters.description: VAN id of the person to update.

scalars.summary: Change a couple of fields, leaving the rest alone

addEmail.summary: Append an email address (existing addresses are kept)

200.description:
Never sent by this endpoint. This is where a redirect-following client *lands* after a successful update:

```
POST /people/102714580         {"firstName": "Cre", …}
  ← 302 Found
    Location: https://api.securevan.com/v4/people/102714580   (same URL)
    {"vanId": 102714580, "status": "Matched"}

GET /people/102714580          ← client re-issues the request at Location
  ← 200 OK
    { the merged record — the body documented here }
```

A happy accident: the update itself never returns the record, but the followed GET does, so redirect-following clients get the merged result for free. See POST /people/find for the full redirect-following notes, including the `curl -X POST -L` gotcha.

The other way to reach a 200 is a failure: when the 302 was the ASP.NET request-validation bounce (a path segment containing `<`, `>`, `*` or `&`), following it lands on the web application's HTML error page, which answers 200 with `text/html`. Check the content type before parsing JSON.

x-provenance.note: Chain observed end to end with httpx: POST /people/{vanId} with an empty body → 302 back to the same URL → GET → 200 with the full record.

302.description:
The record was updated. `Location` points back at the person resource; the body is a match stub, not the updated record.

The same status also covers a failure that never reaches the API: a path segment containing `<`, `>`, `*` or `&` is rejected by ASP.NET request validation and redirected to `/Error.aspx?EID={code}` with an HTML body. Check the content type to tell them apart.

Location.description: URL of the updated person — or of the web application's error page when request validation rejected the path.

x-provenance.note: "Object moved" body of the request-validation redirect; see the RequestValidationRedirect response for the full story.

getUpdatedPerson.description: Fetch the record to see the merged result — the update response does not include it.

get.description: Searches for people matching the given criteria and returns full person records in the standard pagination envelope. At least one search parameter must be set: firstName, lastName, middleName, streetAddress, city, stateOrProvince, zipOrPostalCode, phoneNumber, email, commonName, or officialName. A request with none of these — even one with filter or paging parameters set — returns 400 INVALID_PARAMETER with the text "This endpoint requires at least one search parameter to be set." Text criteria are case-insensitive prefix matches: lastName=Testpers matches "Testperson", lastName=estperson does not. Related collections on the returned records are null unless requested via $expand.

x-provenance.source: van-cli people.ts (list command) plus live sandbox probing; the endpoint is absent from the official docs' page index (llms.txt lists only /people/find).

parameters.name: firstName
parameters.description: First name. Case-insensitive prefix match.

parameters.name: lastName
parameters.description: Last name. Case-insensitive prefix match.

parameters.name: middleName
parameters.description: Middle name.

parameters.name: streetAddress
parameters.description: Street address.

parameters.description: City.

parameters.name: phoneNumber
parameters.description: Phone number. Non-numeric characters are stripped, then the value must be a valid North American number matching `^1?[2-9][0-8]\d[2-9]\d{6,6}$`; anything else returns 400 INVALID_PARAMETER with that regular expression in the hint.

parameters.name: email
parameters.description: Email address. Case-insensitive prefix match, checked against all of the person's email addresses, not just the preferred one.

parameters.name: commonName
parameters.description: Organization common name.

parameters.name: officialName
parameters.description: Organization official name.

parameters.name: contactMode
parameters.description: Filters the results to Person or Organization records. Does not count toward the at-least-one-search-parameter requirement, and any other value is ignored rather than rejected.

parameters.name: employer
parameters.description: Accepted but has no effect on the results, and does not count toward the at-least-one-search-parameter requirement.

x-provenance.note: Listed as a search criterion in van-cli people.ts, but adding it to a lastName search never changed the result count, even for values matching no one. Only My Campaign was probed.

parameters.name: occupation
parameters.description: Accepted but has no effect on the results, and does not count toward the at-least-one-search-parameter requirement.

x-provenance.note: Listed as a search criterion in van-cli people.ts, but adding it to a lastName search never changed the result count, even for values matching no one. Only My Campaign was probed.

parameters.name: dateOfBirth
parameters.description: Accepted but has no effect on the results, and does not count toward the at-least-one-search-parameter requirement. Even an unparseable value is accepted and ignored.

x-provenance.note: Listed as a search criterion in van-cli people.ts, but adding it to a lastName search never changed the result count, even for values matching no one. Only My Campaign was probed.

parameters.name: $top
parameters.description: Limits the number of results per page. Default 50, maximum 200; 0 and negative values return 400.

x-provenance.note: van-cli caps this at 50 client-side with a comment that VAN limits people search to 50, but the API's own INVALID_PARAMETER hint states default 50 / maximum 200, and $top=200 was accepted live.

parameters.name: $skip
parameters.description: Number of results to skip. Negative values return 400.

parameters.name: $orderby
parameters.description: Sort expression. The only sortable property is Name; "Name desc" sorts descending. Any other property returns 400 INVALID_PARAMETER with the hint "The only valid orderby property is: 'Name'".

parameters.name: $expand
parameters.description: Related sections to include, comma-delimited and case-insensitive eg 'addresses,emails' — a much smaller set than GET /people/{vanId} accepts. The API's hint also lists pollingLocation, but requesting it is then refused with 400 BAD_REQUEST "May not request 'pollingLocation' in this context", alone or combined, so the usable set is the four below. Anything outside the hinted set returns 400 INVALID_PARAMETER. Expanded collections come back as empty arrays when absent; unexpanded sections stay null.

x-provenance.note: pollingLocation was rejected in My Campaign mode (the only mode the sandbox key can reach); it may be expandable in My Voters mode, which is what the hint presumably describes.

First of Many Pages (no $expand).description: First of 120 matches for lastName=Testperson with $top=1 (item abridged: null-only fields omitted)

First of Many Pages (with $expand).description: lastName=Testperson&$top=1&$orderby=Name desc&$expand=emails,phones,addresses,districts (item abridged: null-only fields, sandbox fuzz noise, and the duplicate Mailing copy of the address omitted — see GET /people/{vanId} for that quirk)

getFirstPerson.description: Fetch the first matching person's full record (e.g. with the larger $expand set that getPerson accepts).

400.description: Validation error. Most are INVALID_PARAMETER and name the offending query parameter in `properties`; the no-search-parameter case names the pseudo-property "All Arguments", and refusing an out-of-context $expand section uses code BAD_REQUEST with no `properties` or `hint` at all.

x-provenance.note: All five examples are verbatim sandbox responses (My Campaign mode).

'phoneNumber' (555) is not a valid phone number for NorthAmerica

post.summary: Find a person matching the given criteria
post.description: Attempts to match a person in the database. A match returns **302 Found** with a `Location` header pointing at `/people/{vanId}` and a small match-stub body; no match returns **404** with `{"vanId": null, "status": "Unmatched"}`. Sparse criteria (e.g. firstName only) are accepted and simply return Unmatched. Read-only: never creates records (use /people/findOrCreate for that).
post.x-docs-discrepancy: Official docs imply a 200 with a person object on match. Sandbox probing (2026-08-03) shows 302 + Location on match and 404 with a match stub on no match; no 400 was observed even for sparse criteria like firstName-only.

byVanId.summary: Look up by vanId (overrides all other criteria)

200.description:
Never sent by this endpoint. This is where a redirect-following client *lands* on a match:

```
POST /people/find              {"firstName": "Ada", "lastName": "Testperson", …}
  ← 302 Found
    Location: https://api.securevan.com/v4/people/102714507
    {"vanId": 102714507, "status": "Matched"}

GET /people/102714507          ← client re-issues the request at Location
  ← 200 OK
    { full person record — the body documented here }
```

requests, httpx, fetch and `curl -L` all follow that redirect and downgrade POST to GET by default, so a match reaches your code as this 200 and a full `Person`, never as the 302 and its two-field match stub. The no-match 404 is not a redirect, so the practical test is `resp.status_code == 200` vs `404`, not `302` vs `404`. The follow-up GET has no `$expand`, so its related collections come back null — re-fetch through the `getMatchedPerson` link if you need addresses, phones or emails.

Gotcha: `curl -X POST -L` keeps the method across the redirect and re-POSTs to `/people/{vanId}` — the *update* endpoint — where IIS answers `411 Length Required` because the re-issued request carries no body. Drop the explicit `-X POST` (`-d` already implies POST) and curl downgrades to GET like everything else.

x-provenance.note: Chain observed end to end with httpx and requests (both: 302 → GET → 200 Person) and with curl 8.7.1 both ways (`-d` alone → GET → 200; `-X POST -L` → POST /people/{vanId} → 411). Documented alongside the raw 302 so both redirect-following clients and raw clients (including the schemathesis fuzzer) conform to this spec.

matched.summary: Sandbox test person (abridged: null-only fields omitted)

getMatchedPerson.description: Re-fetch the matched person by id (e.g. with $expand for related collections).

302.description: A person matched the criteria. `Location` header points at the canonical person resource.

getMatchedPerson.description: Fetch the matched person's full record — equivalent to following the Location header.

404.description: No person matched the criteria. Body is a match stub with status "Unmatched" (NOT the standard error envelope).

post.summary: Find a person, or create one if nothing matches
post.description:
Runs the same match as POST /people/find and, when nothing matches, stores the payload as a new record.

Outcomes:

- **A record matches** — **302 Found**, with a `Location` header and `{"vanId": …, "status": "Matched"}`.
- **Nothing matches** — **201 Created** with `{"vanId": …, "status": "UnmatchedStored"}`, and the payload is stored as a new record. Unlike find, this never returns 404 — the no-match case is the create case.
- **The body supplies a `vanId` that exists** — the match is short-circuited and that record is returned as **302**.
- **The body is empty (`{}`)** — every field is optional, including the name, so this is a no-match: **201** and a blank record is created.

x-provenance.note: Not in the official docs' page index; the path comes from van-cli (people.ts findOrCreate), which requires firstName and lastName client-side. The API itself requires neither — an empty body was accepted (observed 2026-08-03).

200.description:
Never sent by this endpoint. This is where a redirect-following client *lands* after a match:

```
POST /people/findOrCreate      {"vanId": 102714558}
  ← 302 Found
    Location: https://api.securevan.com/v4/people/102714558
    {"vanId": 102714558, "status": "Matched"}

GET /people/102714558          ← client re-issues the request at Location
  ← 200 OK
    { full person record — the body documented here }
```

So on a match your code sees this 200 and a full `Person`, not the 302 and its two-field match stub. `resp.history` (requests/httpx) or `resp.redirected` (fetch) is how you tell this apart from the 201 create path, which sends no `Location` and is never rewritten this way. See POST /people/find for the full redirect-following notes, including the `curl -X POST -L` gotcha.

x-provenance.note: Chain observed end to end with httpx and requests (both: 302 → GET → 200 Person) and with curl 8.7.1 both ways (`-d` alone → GET → 200; `-X POST -L` → POST /people/{vanId} → 411).

201.description: Nothing matched, so a new record was created. No `Location` header is sent — the new id is in the body, and redirect-following clients see this response unchanged.

getCreatedPerson.description: Fetch the record that was just created.

302.description: An existing person matched, so nothing was written.

getMatchedPerson.description: Fetch the matched person's full record.

post.description:
Stores the payload as a new record and returns **201 Created** with `{"vanId": …, "status": "Stored"}`. No de-duplication happens: posting a name and email identical to an existing record creates a second record. Use POST /people/findOrCreate when you want matching.

The one exception is `vanId`: if the body carries one that exists, nothing is created and the response is **302 Found** for that record, exactly as findOrCreate would answer.

Every field is optional — an empty body `{}` returns 201 and creates a blank record with no name.

x-provenance.note: Not in the official docs' page index; the path comes from van-cli (people.ts create), which requires firstName and lastName client-side. The API requires neither. Duplicate behaviour confirmed by posting an exact copy of an existing person's name and email and receiving a new vanId (observed 2026-08-03).

withDetails.summary: Name plus demographics and contact details

200.description:
Never sent by this endpoint. This is where a redirect-following client *lands* when the body carried a `vanId` that already exists:

```
POST /people/create            {"vanId": 102714558, …}
  ← 302 Found
    Location: https://api.securevan.com/v4/people/102714558
    {"vanId": 102714558, "status": "Matched"}

GET /people/102714558          ← client re-issues the request at Location
  ← 200 OK
    { full person record — the body documented here }
```

So on the vanId path your code sees this 200 and a full `Person` — and, critically, a response that looks nothing like the 201 you get when a record really was created. Check `resp.history` / `resp.redirected`, or just don't send a `vanId` to a create endpoint. See POST /people/find for the full redirect-following notes, including the `curl -X POST -L` gotcha.

x-provenance.note: Chain observed end to end with httpx (302 → GET → 200 Person) by posting an existing vanId; identical to the POST /people/findOrCreate and POST /people/find redirects.

existingVanIdFollowed.summary: What a redirect-following client receives when the posted vanId already exists (abridged: null-only fields omitted)

201.description: A new record was created. No `Location` header is sent — the new id is in the body.

getCreatedPerson.description: Fetch the record that was just created.

302.description: The body carried a vanId that already exists, so nothing was created.

getMatchedPerson.description: Fetch the existing person's full record.

get.description: Returns the context's survey questions, each with its canned responses, in the standard pagination envelope. Every filter is optional; with none set, Active questions are returned. The sandbox committee has no survey questions, so only the empty page has been observed live.

parameters.name: statuses
parameters.description: Statuses to include, comma-delimited. Defaults to Active.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Filters to survey questions whose name starts with the given input.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Filters to survey questions of the given type.

parameters.name: question
parameters.description: Filters to survey questions whose script question contains the given input.

parameters.name: cycle
parameters.description: A year in the format YYYY.

parameters.name: $top
parameters.description: Limits the number of results. Default 50, maximum 200.
parameters.x-docs-discrepancy: Official docs claim a default of 40; the API's own INVALID_PARAMETER hint (observed 2026-08-03) states default 50, maximum 200.

200.description: A paginated list of survey questions.

x-provenance.note: Constructed from official docs; item shape not yet observed live.

items.name: Will Vote 2026
items.scriptQuestion: Can we count on you to vote in the 2026 general election?

post.description: Test endpoint: echoes the posted message back with a server timestamp. Safe to call freely; useful for verifying auth and connectivity. Accepts an empty body (all fields nullable).

delayed.summary: Ask the server to wait before responding

basicAuth.description: HTTP Basic auth. Username = an arbitrary label, e.g. `my_fancy_app`; password = `{apiKey}|{databaseMode}` where databaseMode is `0` (My Voters) or `1` (My Campaign) and apiKey is a UUID like `07540886-b749-433c-b18d-a3d052f6b759`. Using a mode your key lacks returns 401 UNAUTHORIZED "Invalid Database Mode".

MatchedPersonLocation.description: URL of the person the request resolved to.

Forbidden.description: The request was valid but the key's context does not allow it. Observed on GET /people/{vanId} with `$expand=scores`: scores are a My Voters feature, so a My Campaign key is refused even though `scores` is in the API's own list of valid sections. The sibling refusal for `pollingLocation` uses 400 BAD_REQUEST instead — the two are not consistent.

x-provenance.note: Surfaced by the fuzzer once $expand was modelled as an enum of the API's 23 valid sections; each section was then requested in turn against vanId 102714507, and scores was the only 403 (pollingLocation the only 400).

QueryStringTooLong.description: The request never reached the API. IIS rejects any request whose query string runs past roughly 2048 characters and answers with its own HTML "404 - File or directory not found" page, so this 404 means the URL was too long rather than that anything was missing. Nothing in the body identifies the real cause; check the content type, since the API's own 404s are JSON.

x-provenance.note: Found by the fuzzer on GET /surveyQuestions with a very long generated filter value, then bisected with `statuses=AAA…`: 2000 characters still reach the API (which answers 500), 2100 return the IIS 404. Reproduced on GET /people with a long lastName, so this is infrastructure-wide rather than endpoint-specific.

PersonNotFound.description: No person with that vanId exists. Zero and negative ids return this too, as the standard error envelope. Two non-API cases share this status and answer with an IIS HTML page instead: a non-integer path segment, which matches no route, and a query string longer than ~2048 characters, which IIS rejects outright.

errors.text: The specified resource cannot be found.

x-provenance.note: IIS "404 - File or directory not found" page, served when the path segment is not an integer so no API route matches.

RequestValidationRedirect.description:
The request never reached the API. ASP.NET request validation rejects a path segment containing `<`, `>`, `*` or `&` and hands the request to the VAN web application, which answers **302** with `Location: /Error.aspx?EID={code}` and a small HTML "Object moved" body. Clients that follow the redirect land on the web app's HTML "Oops...something went wrong" page with status 200 — HTML, not JSON, from an endpoint that otherwise only speaks JSON.

Other unusual path characters take different routes: `:` and `"` give the IIS HTML 404, and a backslash gives the standard JSON 404 envelope.

x-provenance.note: Found by the stateful fuzz phase on GET /people/{vanId} and reproduced character by character. The EID in the Location is a support reference code; no request data is echoed back.

Location.description: The web application's error page, e.g. /Error.aspx?EID=26B226-343EF8

errors.text: '$top' must be less than or equal to the maximum result size for this end point: 200
errors.hint: If no '$top' parameter is specified, a default top size of 50 will be used.

Unauthorized.description: Missing/invalid API key, or a database mode the key does not have access to.

TooManyRequests.description: Rate limit exceeded. Limits are per API key, set by the key's rate-limit profile, and apply across all endpoints, so any operation can return 429. There is no `Retry-After` header; the suggested wait appears only in the error text ("Try again in N ms."). Unlike other errors, `code` is the numeric string "429" rather than a symbolic name.
TooManyRequests.x-docs-discrepancy: The official docs do not mention rate limiting or the 429 response anywhere in their reference index (checked 2026-08-04). Observed live on GET /surveyQuestions and POST /people/create.

x-provenance.note: Triggered with ~300 concurrent GET /surveyQuestions requests; 225 returned 429. None of them carried a Retry-After header — the retry hint is only in the error text, with the millisecond count varying per response.

errors.text: Rate limit exceeded. Try again in 30 ms.

ServerError.description: Internal server error. The API returns 500 (not 400) for various malformed inputs, e.g. negative delayInMilliseconds on /echoes, non-ASCII filter values on /surveyQuestions, vanId 0 or null phone entries on /people/find, a null phone entry on the person write endpoints, and an `identifiers` entry with the valid type `dwid` on POST /people/create. Two body shapes occur: the standard errors envelope (with a referenceCode for support), or a raw ASP.NET exception payload including a stack trace when the request fails before reaching the API's own error handling (e.g. a query-string key containing '[').

schema.description: The two shapes are disjoint: the standard envelope requires `errors`, the ASP.NET payload requires `message`, and neither carries the other's fields.

aspNet.description: Returned when the request fails before reaching the API's own error handling. `stackTrace` is abridged here; the live response leaks the full trace, including build-server paths.

x-provenance.note: The aspNet example is a verbatim sandbox response to GET /people/102714507?a[=1, with the stack trace truncated after the frames that identify the crash. The internal example is from earlier probing of the malformed inputs listed above.

ErrorResponse.description: The standard error envelope, returned by every failing endpoint except where noted.

code.description: Machine-readable error code. Known values: UNAUTHORIZED, FORBIDDEN, INVALID_PARAMETER, BAD_REQUEST, NOT_FOUND, METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED, INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR (list likely incomplete).

properties.description: JSON paths of the offending request properties, e.g. "responses[0].shortName".

hint.description: How to fix it — often the accepted values or a regular expression.

referenceCode.description: Support reference code; present on INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR responses.

AspNetError.description: Raw ASP.NET Web API exception payload, returned on some 500s instead of the standard errors envelope when the request fails before reaching the API's own error handling — e.g. a query-string key containing '[' crashes jQuery-syntax key parsing. Includes a full stack trace.

x-provenance.note: Found by the stateful fuzz phase on GET /people/{vanId} with a fuzzed query-string key containing '['. The stack-trace disclosure is itself a VAN bug, logged in STATUS.md.

EchoRequest.description: A message to send to the echo endpoint. Every field is optional.

delayInMilliseconds.description: Optional server-side delay before responding, in milliseconds. Warning: -1 hangs the connection indefinitely; other negative values return 500.

x-provenance.note: The -1 hang is likely the value being passed straight to .NET as Timeout.Infinite. Spec minimum is 1 so fuzzer boundary probes send 0 (safe) rather than -1.

Echo.description: The posted message, echoed back with a server timestamp.

dateSent.description: Server time when the response was produced.

delayInMilliseconds.description: The delay that was applied, echoed back.

PersonMatchCriteria.description: Match criteria. A valid vanId overrides all other criteria.

vanId.description: VAN id of the person; a valid vanId overrides all other criteria. Warning: the API returns 500 for vanId 0.

phones.description: Phone numbers to match on. A null array entry returns 500.

PersonMatchEmail.description: An email address used as match criteria — the address only, unlike the fuller PersonEmailInput used when writing.

PersonMatchPhone.description: A phone number used as match criteria — no type or opt-in fields, unlike the PersonPhoneInput used when writing.

countryCode.x-docs-discrepancy: Official docs spell this field 'countyCode' — likely a typo in the docs; not yet verified live.

PersonMatched.description: An existing record was found and nothing was written. The only match-stub shape that accompanies a 302: from find, findOrCreate, create when the body's vanId exists, and update.

PersonUnmatched.description: Nothing matched and nothing was written — the 404 body from find. The one match-stub shape with a null vanId.

PersonUnmatchedStored.description: Nothing matched, so a new record was created — the 201 body from findOrCreate.

PersonStored.description: A new record was created with no attempt to match — the 201 body from create.

Page.description: The envelope every paginated endpoint returns around its `items` array.

nextPageLink.description: Absolute URL of the next page — including an explicit `:443` port — or null on the last page.

count.description: Total number of matches across all pages, not the size of this page.

x-provenance.note: Item shape derived from official docs; not yet observed live — the sandbox committee has no survey questions and POST /surveyQuestions rejects every type value tried so far.

type.description: Category of question, e.g. "GOTV". The full set of values is not known — POST /surveyQuestions rejected every type tried in the sandbox.

cycle.description: Election year the question belongs to, as YYYY.

mediumName.description: Abbreviated name, for displays with limited room.

shortName.description: Shortest form of the name, for the tightest displays.

scriptQuestion.description: The question as read aloud to the person.

status.description: Whether the question is in use.

x-provenance.note: Enum inferred from the values the `statuses` filter accepts; never observed on a live item.

responses.description: The canned answers a canvasser can record against this question.

SurveyQuestionStatus.description: `Active` — in use. `Archived` — retired but kept for reporting. `Inactive` — not currently in use.

SurveyQuestionResponse.description: A canned answer to a survey question.

name.description: Full text of the answer, e.g. "Yes".

shortName.description: Shortest form of the answer, e.g. "Y".

PersonEmail.description: An email address on a person record, returned when $expand=emails is requested.

x-provenance.note: Enums taken from the API's own INVALID_PARAMETER responses to POST /people/findOrCreate and confirmed by round-tripping every value through GET /people/{vanId}?$expand=emails. Unlike phones, email codes come back as the same single letters that were written. Nullability probed 2026-08-04: an email written with only the address, and another written with every optional field explicitly null, both read back fully populated with defaults (type P, isPreferred, subscriptionStatus S) — isSubscribed is the only field observed null.

type.description: What kind of address this is. `P` = personal, `W` = work, `O` = other. Defaults to `P` when not set at write time, so it is never null.

x-provenance.note: Writing any other value returns 400 INVALID_PARAMETER: "'type' must be one of P , W , O". Writing an explicit null reads back as "P" (observed 2026-08-04).

dateCreated.description: When the address was added to the record. Set by the server.

isPreferred.description: Whether this is the person's preferred email address. Exactly one address per person carries it.

isSubscribed.description: The pre-Targeted-Email view of `subscriptionStatus`: whether the address may be used in a broadcast email. Derived from `subscriptionStatus` — `S` maps to true, `U` to false, and `N` to null, since neutral has no boolean equivalent.

x-provenance.note: The S/U/N -> true/false/null mapping was observed by writing each subscriptionStatus and reading the record back (2026-08-03). The docs describe isSubscribed only as a write field and mark it deprecated where Targeted Email is available; they do not say what it reads back as.

subscriptionStatus.description: Targeted Email subscription state. `S` = subscribed — the default at write time, and the only status that receives Targeted Email messages. `N` = neutral — no message, but not an opt-out. `U` = unsubscribed. Null on some addresses (`isSubscribed` is null there too). This property exists only where the Targeted Email feature is enabled.

x-provenance.note: Writing any other value returns 400 INVALID_PARAMETER with hint "'U', 'S', 'N'". An email written without it (or with an explicit null) reads back "S" (2026-08-04), but the fuzzer's mutation target carries four older non-preferred addresses whose status reads null — the rule that nulls it was not pinned down, so null stays in the schema.

PersonPhone.description: A phone number on a person record, returned when $expand=phones is requested.

x-provenance.note: Shape and every enum observed live: each documented write code was posted through POST /people/findOrCreate and read back via GET /people/{vanId}?$expand=phones. Fields not in the documented model (dateCreated, isBest, isDisclosure, smsOptInStatus, isCellPhoneExchange, tags) are read-only additions seen on every phone returned. Nullability probed 2026-08-04: a phone written with only phoneNumber, and another written with every optional field explicitly null, both read back fully populated — the server substitutes defaults (phoneType Personal, deviceType Unknown, opt-in statuses Unknown, dialingPrefix/countryCode from the context) — so only ext, isCellStatus and tags are ever null.

phoneId.description: Read-only; unique identifier of the phone.

phoneNumber.description: The number, normalized to digits only. Required and validated at write time, so never null.

dialingPrefix.description: 1 to 3 digit country dialing prefix, e.g. "1" for North America. Derived from the number's country (defaulting to the context's country) when not written.

countryCode.description: ISO alpha-2 code of the country the number belongs to, e.g. "US". Derived from the number's country (defaulting to the context's country) when not written.

ext.description: Extension; no more than six numeric characters.

dateCreated.description: When the number was added to the record. Set by the server.

phoneType.description: Which sphere of the person's life the number belongs to. Defaults to `Personal` when no type is written, so it is never null. The cell/fax/landline/etc distinction is stored in `deviceType`, not here.

x-provenance.note: Mapping established by writing all seven accepted codes to one record and reading them back (2026-08-03). Enum lists the read values observed for those codes; records created outside the API were not sampled. Phones written with no phoneType, or with an explicit null, read back "Personal" (observed 2026-08-04).

phoneType.x-docs-discrepancy: Official docs document only the write codes and imply they are echoed back. GET returns an expanded category name instead, and seven write codes collapse onto three of them (observed 2026-08-03).

deviceType.description: What physical kind of device answers the number (decides if the number is textable). "Unknown" when the device kind has never been established.

x-provenance.note: Read values confirmed by writing each of C, L, U, F, V and reading back (2026-08-03).

deviceType.x-docs-discrepancy: Official docs document only the write codes C, L, U, F, V and imply they are echoed back; GET returns the spelled-out names Cell/Landline/Unknown/Fax/VoIP (observed 2026-08-03).

isPreferred.description: Whether this is the person's preferred phone number. At most one number per person carries it.

x-provenance.note: Records with several phones never showed more than one preferred; whether a record with phones always has exactly one was not established.

isBest.description: Read-only; whether this is the best known number of its type — the most recently updated one.

isDisclosure.description: Read-only; whether the number is usable for campaign-finance disclosure reporting.

x-provenance.note: Not in the documented model. Observed true on the first number written to a record and on numbers written with deviceType Cell, false otherwise; the exact rule was not pinned down.

smsOptInStatus.description: Read-only; text-message consent for this number. "Unknown" — never null — when no consent has been recorded.

x-provenance.note: Not in the documented model. Observed to mirror phoneOptInStatus on every phone probed (2026-08-03); there is no separate write field for it.

phoneOptInStatus.description: Whether the person has consented to being contacted at this number. "Unknown" — never null — when no consent has been recorded.

x-provenance.note: Writing any other value returns 400 INVALID_PARAMETER: "'phoneOptInStatus' must be one of I , U , O".

phoneOptInStatus.x-docs-discrepancy: Official docs describe the field only as the write codes I/U/O; GET returns the expanded names Opt-In/Unknown/Opt-Out (observed 2026-08-03).

isCellPhoneExchange.description: Read-only; whether the number's exchange (area code + prefix) is one allocated to wireless carriers. An inference from the number itself, independent of `deviceType` and `isCellStatus`.

x-provenance.note: Not in the documented model. Only observed as false — the sandbox's fictional 555 numbers belong to no real exchange.

isCellStatus.description: How confident VAN is that this number reaches a cell phone. Null when no explicit status has been applied.
isCellStatus.x-docs-discrepancy: The value written is validated but never read back: phones written with a valid isCellStatus still return null from GET /people/{vanId}?$expand=phones (observed 2026-08-03).

tags.description: Read-only; tags applied to the number.

x-provenance.note: Not in the documented model. Only observed as null; item shape unverified.

PhoneIsCellStatus.description: A confidence level for whether a phone number reaches a cell phone. The four levels are fixed; `GET /phones/isCellStatuses` returns them as a bare array (empty in the sandbox). On write, supplying either `statusId` or `statusName` alone is enough; omitting the object entirely leaves any existing status unchanged.

x-provenance.note: Values come from the API's own INVALID_PARAMETER response: "'statusId' must be one of 1 , 2 , 3 , 4" and "'statusName' must be one of Verified Cell , Likely Cell , Likely Not a Cell , Not a Cell". The id-to-name pairing below follows that ordering and the docs' example ({"statusId": 2, "statusName": "Likely Cell"}); the API accepts a mismatched pair without complaint, so the pairing could not be confirmed by round-trip.

PersonAddress.description: An address on a person record, returned when $expand=addresses is requested. The expansion returns the best known Home address and the best known Mailing address only — at most two entries, and the same address appears twice (once per type, sharing an addressId) when it serves as both. Work and Custom addresses are stored but not surfaced here.

x-provenance.note: Shape observed live by writing addresses of each documented type through POST /people/findOrCreate and reading them back. Fields not in the documented model (unitNo, geoLocation, preview, streetAddress, displayMode) are read-only additions seen on every address returned. Nullability probed 2026-08-04: a zip-only address reads back with city/state inferred from the zip and addressLine1 null; a city+state-only address reads back zipOrPostalCode "" (empty string, not null); addresses too sparse or unresolvable to standardize (street line only, or an unknown zip) are not surfaced by the expansion at all — so city, stateOrProvince, zipOrPostalCode and countryCode were never observed null.

addressId.description: Read-only; unique identifier of the address on this person. Shared by the Home and Mailing entries when one address fills both roles.

addressLine1.description: First line of the standardized street address.

addressLine2.description: Second line of the street address.

addressLine3.description: Third line of the street address.

unitNo.description: Read-only; the unit or apartment number parsed out of the street address by standardization.

x-provenance.note: Not in the documented model. Only observed as null, including for an address written with "Apt 4" on line 2 — the sandbox does not appear to run full standardization.

city.description: City or town. Inferred from the postal code when not written.

stateOrProvince.description: Two or three character state or province code, e.g. "MN", "ON", "NSW". Inferred from the postal code when not written.

zipOrPostalCode.description: ZIP, ZIP+4, postal code, post code, etc. An empty string — not null — when the stored address has none.

geoLocation.description: Read-only; the geocoded position of the address.

x-provenance.note: Not in the documented model. Only observed as null — the sandbox does not geocode API-created addresses; type unverified.

countryCode.description: Two character ISO country code supported by the VAN context, e.g. "US". Defaults to the context's country.

preview.description: Read-only; a one-line display form of the street address. A single space when there are no street lines.

x-provenance.note: Not in the documented model. Observed as address lines 1 and 2 joined by a space, with a trailing space when line 2 is empty.

type.description: Which role the address plays for the person. This expansion only ever returns "Voting" or "Mailing"; a person with no mailing address of their own has their home address returned under "Mailing" as well.

x-provenance.note: Read values observed by writing Home, Work, Mailing and Custom addresses (2026-08-03). An address written as Work or Custom did not appear in the expansion at all.

type.x-docs-discrepancy: Official docs list five address types with no indication that reads are restricted; $expand=addresses only ever returns Voting and Mailing, and Work and Custom addresses are omitted from the response entirely (observed 2026-08-03).

isPreferred.description: Read-only; whether this is the person's preferred address.

isBest.description: Read-only; whether this is the best known address of its type — the most recently updated one.

streetAddress.description: Read-only; the street portion of the standardized address.

x-provenance.note: Not in the documented model. Only observed as null; type assumed to be string.

displayMode.description: Read-only; which form of the address the other fields show — "Standardized" for the normalized version rather than the raw text as entered.

x-provenance.note: Not in the documented model. Only "Standardized" observed; other values not enumerated, so this is left unconstrained.

PersonEmailInput.description: An email address as written to a person record. Reads come back as PersonEmail; the two differ only in required-ness and the server-set dateCreated, since email codes round-trip unchanged.

x-provenance.note: Every value round-tripped through POST /people/findOrCreate and GET /people/{vanId}?$expand=emails.

email.description: The address. Validated: a malformed value returns 400 INVALID_PARAMETER "'email' is not a valid email address".

isPreferred.description: Whether this becomes the person's preferred address. Documented as defaulting to false, but the flag moves to the most recently added address on its own: writing three addresses in turn without ever setting this leaves only the newest preferred. Phones do not behave this way — an unflagged phone stays unpreferred.

x-provenance.note: Observed by appending three emails to one record in separate requests, none setting isPreferred, and seeing the flag follow the newest each time (2026-08-03).

isSubscribed.description: Deprecated where Targeted Email is available. `false` is a permanent opt-out — it stores `subscriptionStatus: "U"`, which cannot be reversed. Cannot be sent together with `subscriptionStatus`.

subscriptionStatus.description: `S` = subscribed (the default, and the only status that receives Targeted Email), `N` = neutral, `U` = unsubscribed. `U` is terminal. Only available where Targeted Email is enabled, and not valid alongside `isSubscribed`.

PersonPhoneInput.description: A phone number as written to a person record. The code fields take single letters here, but they are input codes mapped to the stored model at write time (see PersonPhone): several codes collapse onto one stored value, and reads return the stored words, not the codes.

x-provenance.note: Every code round-tripped through POST /people/findOrCreate and GET /people/{vanId}?$expand=phones.

phoneNumber.description: Non-numeric characters are stripped, then the remaining digits are validated for the country implied by `countryCode`/`dialingPrefix`, defaulting to the context's country. A number that fails validation returns 400 INVALID_PARAMETER "Phone number is not valid. If entering UK number, please include leading 0.".

phoneType.description: `H` = home, `W` = work, `O` = other, `C` = cell, `M` = main, `F` = fax, `P` = personal. A write-only input code, not what is stored: at write time it is collapsed and stored as `phoneType` `Personal` (H, C, M, P), `Work` (W, F) or `Other` (O), and `C` additionally stores `deviceType: "Cell"` while `F` stores `deviceType: "Fax"`. Reads return the stored values (see PersonPhone).
phoneType.x-docs-discrepancy: Official docs list five codes (H, W, C, M, F); the API's own INVALID_PARAMETER response accepts seven — "'phoneType' must be one of: H, W, O, C, M, F, P" (observed 2026-08-03).

deviceType.description: What kind of device answers the number; decides whether it is textable. Accepts either a letter — `C` = cell, `L` = landline, `U` = unknown, `F` = fax, `V` = VoIP — or the equivalent numeric id: 1 (Cell), 2 (Landline), 4 (Unknown), 5 (Fax), 6 (VoIP). Defaults to Unknown. Available since May 9, 2024.
deviceType.x-docs-discrepancy: Official docs list only the letter codes. The API's INVALID_PARAMETER response also accepts numeric ids 1, 2, 4, 5, 6; writing 2 and 6 was confirmed to store Landline and VoIP (observed 2026-08-03). There is no id 3.

ext.description: Extension. Over six characters returns 400 INVALID_PARAMETER "'ext' must be between 0 and 6 characters".

isPreferred.description: Whether this becomes the person's preferred number. Defaults to false and stays there — unlike emails, a newly added phone does not take the preferred flag from the existing one.

x-provenance.note: Seven phones written to one record with no isPreferred flag all read back isPreferred false (2026-08-03).

phoneOptInStatus.description: `I` = opt in, `U` = unknown (the default), `O` = opt out. Reads back as `Opt-In`, `Unknown`, `Opt-Out`, and also sets the read-only `smsOptInStatus` to the same value.

isCellStatus.description: Confidence that the number reaches a cell phone. Omitting it leaves any existing explicit status unchanged.

dialingPrefix.description: 1 to 3 numeric characters identifying the country, e.g. "1". If sent alongside `countryCode`, the two must name the same country.

countryCode.description: ISO alpha-2 country code, e.g. "US". If sent alongside `dialingPrefix`, the two must name the same country.

PersonAddressInput.description: An address as written to a person record. Reads come back as PersonAddress, which surfaces only the best known Home and Mailing addresses and adds several standardization fields.

x-provenance.note: Each documented type written through POST /people/findOrCreate and read back with $expand=addresses.

addressLine1.description: First line of the street address.

addressLine2.description: Second line of the street address.

addressLine3.description: Third line of the street address.

stateOrProvince.description: Two or three character state or province code, e.g. "MN", "ON", "NSW".

zipOrPostalCode.description: ZIP, ZIP+4, postal code, post code, etc.

countryCode.description: Two character ISO country code supported by the VAN context. Defaults to the context's country.

type.description: `Home` and `Voting` mean the same thing and read back as `Voting`. Some types are unavailable in some contexts. An address written as `Work` or `Custom` is stored but never appears under $expand=addresses. When a person has no mailing address, their home address serves as the mailing address too.
type.x-docs-discrepancy: The value is not validated: an address written with type "Q" is accepted with 201 and filed as the person's home address (observed 2026-08-03).

PersonIdentifierInput.description: A known external identifier for the person, e.g. a DWID or voter file VANID. External IDs are case-insensitive in VAN — "Abcd1234" always matches "ABCD1234".

x-provenance.note: Only the rejection path was observed: an unrecognized type returns 400 "'type' (bogus) is not a valid ExternalID in this context". The sandbox 500s on the valid type 'dwid' (see the operation description), so a successful write was never observed.

type.description: An external identifier type available in the current context. Use `votervanid` for a VoterFile VANID from a My Campaign call, and `dwid` for Catalist DWIDs in either mode.

PersonCustomFieldValueInput.description: A value for one of the context's custom fields.

x-provenance.note: Only the rejection path was observed — the demo committee defines no custom fields, so writing customFieldId 1 returns 400 "Custom field 1 does not exist.". Property names taken from the error's `properties` path and the official docs.

customFieldId.description: Id of a custom field defined in the current context. Unknown ids return 400 INVALID_PARAMETER.

customFieldGroupId.description: Id of the custom field's group.

PersonInput.description: The person payload shared by POST /people/create, POST /people/findOrCreate and POST /people/{vanId} — called the "Match Candidate" common model in the official docs. Every field is optional — an entirely empty body is accepted and creates a blank record. On update the payload is merged, not replaced: fields left out keep their existing values, and emails, phones and addresses are appended rather than swapped.

x-provenance.note: Field list from the official docs' Match Candidate model; max lengths and the enforced/unenforced split established by probing POST /people/create with out-of-range values. Not modelled here, because the sandbox has no lookup values to write against and only the 400 path could be seen: pronouns, selfReportedRaces, selfReportedEthnicities, selfReportedGenders, selfReportedSexualOrientations and selfReportedLanguagePreference. Each takes an id that must exist in the context, e.g. 'reportedRaceId' is not a valid ReportedRace in this context.

vanId.description: Id of an existing record. When it matches, all other criteria are ignored and the endpoint returns 302 Matched instead of creating anything — this is the only way POST /people/create will decline to create a record. A vanId of 0, or one matching nothing, is silently ignored and a new record is created.

x-provenance.note: Unlike POST /people/find, which returns 500 for vanId 0, the write endpoints tolerate it (observed 2026-08-03), so no minimum is imposed here.

suffix.description: Part of the name following the last name, e.g. "Jr.".

salutation.description: Preferred greeting for correspondence. Derived from the name when not supplied.

envelopeName.description: Preferred name for mailings. Derived from the name when not supplied.

party.description: One-character party affiliation, e.g. "D". Only the length is checked — any single character is stored as given.

x-provenance.note: Writing "Q" is accepted and reads back as "Q"; writing "Democrat" returns 400 for length, not for value (observed 2026-08-03).

contactMethodPreferenceCode.description: Preferred method of contact: `P` = phone, `E` = email, `M` = mail, `F` = fax, `S` = SMS. Any other value returns 400 "The specified condition was not met for 'contactMethodPreferenceCode'".

employer.description: May not be available in every context.

occupation.description: May not be available in every context.

jobTitle.description: May not be available in every context.

sex.description: Matched case-insensitively — "m" is accepted and stored as "M". Any other value returns 400 "The specified condition was not met for 'sex'".

dateOfBirth.description: ISO 8601 date, which must fall in the 20th or 21st century — otherwise 400 "'dateOfBirth' must be in the 20th or 21st century.". A value that is not a parseable date is not an error: it is silently dropped and the record stores null.

x-provenance.note: "not-a-date" returned 201 with dateOfBirth null (observed 2026-08-03).

collectedLocationId.description: Location where the person's voter registration application was collected.

electionType.description: Type of election registered for: `G` = General, `P` = Primary, `R` = Run-off, `PP` = Presidential Primary, `SP` = Special Primary, `SG` = Special General, `MP` = Municipal Primary, `MG` = Municipal General, `C` = Caucus, `O` = Other. Any other value returns 400 "Invalid Election Type".

cycle.description: Election year the person registered to vote, as a four-character numeric string. Any other length returns 400 "'cycle' must be 4 characters in length".

emails.description: Appended to the record's existing addresses, not substituted for them. A bare object instead of an array is silently ignored.

phones.description: Appended to the record's existing numbers, not substituted for them. A bare object instead of an array is silently ignored. A null array entry returns 500.

addresses.description: Appended to the record's existing addresses, not substituted for them. A bare object instead of an array is silently ignored.

identifiers.description: Known external identifiers. Writing a type the context does not recognize returns a clean 400; writing the valid type `dwid` returns 500 in a My Campaign context, so no successful write was ever observed.

organizationContactCommonName.description: An organization's common name. Only applies to My Campaign databases with organizations-as-contacts enabled.

organizationContactOfficialName.description: An organization's official name. Only applies to My Campaign databases with organizations-as-contacts enabled.

contactMode.description: Only applies to My Campaign databases with organizations-as-contacts enabled.
contactMode.x-docs-discrepancy: Official docs say the value must be Person or Organization; it is not validated. Writing "Q" returns 201 and the record reads back with contactMode "Person" (observed 2026-08-03).

Person.description:
A person record: returned by GET /people/{vanId}, as the items of GET /people, and as what a redirect-following client lands on after the write endpoints. A few fields read differently between get-by-id and search — see `formalSalutation` and `formalEnvelopeName`.

The properties listed below with no type were only ever observed as null, either because the section needs `$expand` or because the sandbox committee holds no such data. They are listed to document that the API returns them, but their shape is unverified.

x-provenance.note: Field inventory observed live on a minimal API-created record; the untyped fields need a richer record to pin down. Nullability checked against a fully blank record (created from {}, 2026-08-04): even there contactSource, contactMode, formalSalutation ("Friend"), formalEnvelopeName ("Our Friend At"), isDeceased, dateCreated and dateAcquired come back populated, while salutation and envelopeName are null.

contactSource.description: How the record entered the database, e.g. "API".

x-provenance.note: Only "API" observed (the sandbox has no UI-created records); other values not enumerated. Present even on a blank record, so typed non-null.

contactMode.description: Defaults to "Person" even on a blank record; an unrecognized written value is stored as "Person".

formalSalutation.description: On GET /people/{vanId}, derived from the name — "Friend" when there is no name to derive from, unlike `salutation`, which is null in that case. Always null in GET /people search results, even for records where get-by-id derives a value.

x-provenance.note: Null-in-search-results found by the fuzzer on GET /people; confirmed against vanId 102704536, which reads back "Scgapi Matchrules" here via get-by-id but null via search.

formalEnvelopeName.description: On GET /people/{vanId}, derived from the name — "Our Friend At" when there is no name to derive from, unlike `envelopeName`, which is null in that case. Always null in GET /people search results, even for records where get-by-id derives a value.

x-provenance.note: Null-in-search-results found by the fuzzer on GET /people; same evidence as formalSalutation.

sex.description: Always the uppercase one-letter code, even when the record was written with a lowercase value.

x-provenance.source: sandbox probe + official docs (common-models.md: "must be M or F")
x-provenance.note: Wrote sex "m"/"f" via /people/findOrCreate; GET returned "M"/"F" respectively (vanIds 102716311, 102716312).

partialDateOfBirth.description: The birth date broken into components; null when dateOfBirth is null. Returned by both GET /people and GET /people/{vanId}.

x-provenance.note: Surfaced by fuzzing GET /people — earlier field inventories missed it because every probed record had a null dateOfBirth, which nulls this field too. Only full dates observed (month, day and year all set); whether a genuinely partial date omits components is unverified.

dateAcquired.description: For API-created records this is "0001-01-01T00:00:00Z" (the .NET default date).

emails.description: Null unless the request included $expand=emails; an empty array when expanded and none exist.

phones.description: Null unless the request included $expand=phones; an empty array when expanded and none exist. Every phone on the record is returned, not just the best known one.

addresses.description: Null unless the request included $expand=addresses; an empty array when expanded and none exist. Provides the best known Home address and the best known Mailing address only — the same address appears under both types when it fills both roles, and Work/Custom addresses are omitted.
